results.title: Count islands in a square grid
results.expected_rationale: The outer loops inspect n² cells; each land cell is enqueued at most once and each BFS step checks four neighbors.
results.explanation: Recognized full-grid scanning with component BFS, shared visited state, and four constant-time neighbor checks per enqueued cell. Each cell is enqueued at most once across all component scans, yielding O(n^2). This is a bounded AST heuristic, not a proof for arbitrary Python control flow. Called helper functions are not included; this estimate is not a proof.

bfs_evidence.bounded_work_argument: The outer loops inspect R*C cells. The visited set is shared across all component scans, each land cell is enqueued at most once, and each dequeued cell checks exactly four neighbors; total queue and neighbor work is O(R*C).
assumptions: The two outer loops enumerate each grid cell once.
The visited set is not cleared between component searches.
Set membership/addition and deque operations are average O(1).
Grid indexing and the four neighbor checks are O(1).
limitations: This recognizes only explicit four-neighbor component BFS with tuple coordinates.
This is a bounded syntax heuristic, not a proof for arbitrary Python control flow.
Called helper work and alias-based mutation are not expanded.

note: Approved calibration data used to develop this rule; not an untouched holdout. This static result is a bounded syntax heuristic, not a formal proof or timing measurement.
